title: Responsive Typography
definition: Using breakpoints to change font sizes (`text-*`), ensuring text is readable on phones but correctly scaled up for massive monitors.
simpleExplanation: A `text-6xl` Hero Header looks magnificent on a 27-inch iMac. If you load that exact same header on an iPhone, the word 'Welcome' will be so huge it will break onto 3 different lines and ruin the screen. You must use `text-3xl md:text-6xl`.
realWorldExample: Creating a blog post where the main paragraph text is `text-base` (16px) on mobile, but jumps to `text-lg` (18px) on laptops for easier reading from further away.

basic: What Tailwind pattern ensures a heading is small on mobile but huge on desktop?
intermediate: Does changing the font size responsively (e.g., `md:text-xl`) also automatically update the line-height responsively in Tailwind?

answers.question: Which pattern?
answers.answer: `text-2xl md:text-5xl` (Or any similar combination of small base class + larger prefixed class).

answers.question: Line-height update?
answers.answer: Yes! Because Tailwind pairs every `text-*` class with a matching `line-height` by default, changing the text size automatically recalculates the optimal line height for that specific breakpoint.
